summary: Calumet Light, Columbia Park, Lake Winnebago: a Fond du Lac factory water tower moved to the harbor in 1936. Owned by Fond du Lac County; climbable.

access.note: Grounds and tower open (LighthouseFriends). Owned by Fond du Lac County. Check county hours before going up.

events.note: Moved from its factory site to Calumet Harbor and converted to an observation tower and navigation aid.
Wooden staircase and observation decks had deteriorated by the early 1980s and were removed.
Restored by the Columbia Park Tower Fund and Fond du Lac County and reopened for climbing.

notes_for_editor: THIN STORY. Four independent sources bear on the tower (LighthouseFriends, Friends of the Fox, two 1908 and 1931 newspapers); nothing in the corpus or federal reports names this tower. (1) Do not use the USLHS roster for 'Calumet Harbor, IL' (81 lines, 1906-1966). That place is Calumet Harbor, Illinois, on Lake Michigan (Cook County). The USLHS place record carries this Wisconsin position (43.9133, -88.33), which is why the roster matcher picked it. No keepers are attached to this station; 'keepers' is empty. (2) Characteristic: the record says 'Fl W 6s'. Wikipedia's lead gives 'two flashing white' (leads only). No source read confirms either, so the story does not state a characteristic. (3) County: LighthouseFriends says Pipe is in 'Calumet County' and the place is in the town of Pipe. Friends of the Fox and LighthouseFriends' visitor notes give Fond du Lac County ownership. The record's Fond du Lac County is used. (4) Heights: 75 ft (LighthouseFriends), 70 ft (Friends of the Fox), 21.0 m (record). (5) The Facebook and Pinterest posts that mention a WPA project were not used. The WPA claim is unsourced. (6) The record's name 'Calumet Light' and the place name 'Columbia Park' are both used. (7) No photos mirrored. Wikipedia and Grokipedia were read as leads only and are not cited. (8) The 1936 move is sourced to LighthouseFriends and Friends of the Fox; the 1936 date is consistent across both. No federal or county record of the move was found. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28 (Haiku 5.5): THIN STORY, still thin. Each footnoted sentence was checked against the cached LighthouseFriends and Friends of the Fox pages and the three newspaper pages. Corrections: the story no longer places the light in Fond du Lac County. LighthouseFriends says the town of Pipe is in Calumet County, and no source read says where the light is in county terms; the story says only that Fond du Lac County owns it. The bank closure is given as 12 January with no year, because the paper gives no year for it; the 1931 date belongs to the reopening report. The December 1931 item is now a hearing: the Leader says war department engineers 'will bear pleas' (the OCR; the headline says 'Pleas Will Be Heard'), in the federal building 'here' on 2 January. The dateline is not in the OCR text read, so 'here' is taken as Fond du Lac (the paper's Fond du Lac river and Lakeside park items point the same way); a human should check the page image. The story now says 'government inspectors of steamboats' where it had said 'federal'; the 1908 paper says 'government'. The $53,000 and $45,000 figures are cited to LighthouseFriends alone. The 'small' harbour is now footnoted to LighthouseFriends. The visiting-hours advice is replaced by a statement that the sources give no hours. Heights: 75 ft (LighthouseFriends, 23 m) and 70 ft (Friends of the Fox, 21 m) are both kept, unchosen. The Watertown OCR reads 'now steamer' for the steamer's name line; the story omits the adjective and quotes the OCR as printed in evidence.
